evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.limitation: The scenario tuple for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' is not present anywhere in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md (it lives in scripts//tests/, which this runbook forbids reading). The scenario inputs below were therefore RECONSTRUCTED by inverting the two golden values against the cached wiki stats, not read from the scenario definition.

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json — {{rd|X|Y}} template semantics established by corpus cross-check
sources_quoted.text: Ravenous Hydra / Tiamat / Stridebreaker 'Cleave' = {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}; Titanic Hydra 'Cleave' = {{rd|1%|{{fd|0.5}}...}} => {{rd|melee|ranged}}: first value is the melee holder's, second the ranged holder's. Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is therefore 8% for a melee holder, 5% for a ranged holder.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md 2.2 'Penetration and reduction order: exact composition'
sources_quoted.text: R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f)   [percentage armor reduction acts on the target's armor value]

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md 2.3 item 3 (League Wiki 'Armor penetration' quoted therein)
sources_quoted.text: "Flat armor reduction can reduce armor values below 0, while percentage armor reduction cannot." — reduction is a property of the TARGET's armor value (a debuff), unlike penetration, which is attacker-local.
the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch) ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C

step_0_ratio_is_the_invariant.note: Without the scenario tuple, the recoverable quantity is the ratio, which is independent of the raw damage.

step_1_rule_out_every_armor_reduction_MO.method: For a change from reduction rho_old to rho_new at target armor A, ratio = (100 + rho_old_eff*A)/(100 + rho_new_eff*A) with rho_eff = 1 - rho. Solve for A and compare with the maximum achievable no-item champion armor.
results: 24% (0.8*max_stacks constant, S7) -> 30% (5 stacks, S1): requires A = 2173 armor. Impossible.
18% (Cesaro at h=5) -> 30%: requires A = 5214 armor. Impossible.
12% (hits/2 short-fight branch) -> 24%: ratio < 1 in the required direction. Impossible.
0% -> 24%: requires A = 147.3; maximum no-item champion armor in data/champions.json is 141.2 (Sejuani, level 20). Not reachable without armor items.
0% -> 30%: requires A in [90.0, 91.9] for the rounding band. REACHABLE.
step_1_rule_out_every_armor_reduction_MO.conclusion: The +16.7% jump cannot come from re-tuning how many Carve stacks are averaged; it can only come from a damage instance that previously saw UNSHREDDED armor now seeing the full 5-stack, 30% Carve reduction (S1).

step_2_recover_the_input_tuple_by_invers.search: Swept all 173 champions x levels 18 and 20 as attacker (base AD + 40 AD from Black Cleaver, S10) x all 173 champions x levels 18/20 as target (armor, S8 growth formula) x Expose Weakness amp in {none, 5%, 8%} (S2/S3), requiring round(raw*100/(100+A),1) == 94.1 AND round(raw*100/(100+0.7A),1) == 109.8.

unique_solution_at_level_18.amp: Bloodsong 'Expose Weakness', ranged holder = 5% increased damage from all sources (present on BOTH sides of the change)

arithmetic: for reference, the 0.8*max_stacks average model (24%, armor 69.16) would give 106.297 -> 106.3, which is NOT either golden value
step_2_recover_the_input_tuple_by_invers.caveat: The champion identities are an inversion result, not a read of the scenario file; the verdict does not depend on them. What is load-bearing is that (a) the exact ratio equals (100+A)/(100+0.7A) at A = 91.0, an exact level-18 champion armor, and (b) no reduction-model re-tuning can produce this ratio at any reachable armor.

step_3_which_value_the_wiki_demands.rule: Carve is an ARMOR REDUCTION debuff placed on the enemy champion (S1). Per S5/S6, percentage armor reduction modifies the target's own armor value, so every incoming physical damage instance from ANY source is mitigated at the reduced armor - unlike penetration, which is attacker-local. Likewise Bloodsong's Expose Weakness explicitly amplifies damage 'from all sources' (S2), i.e. across the roster.
step_3_which_value_the_wiki_demands.therefore: In a coupled roster fight the pair partner's physical damage against a 5-stack Carve target must be mitigated at 0.7*A, not A. Event index 59 is deep into the fight, far past the 5 physical hits needed to cap Carve, and the 6-second stack duration exceeds any realistic inter-event interval (S7), so full 30% is the correct per-event state.
step_3_which_value_the_wiki_demands.old_value_94.1: mitigated at the FULL 91.00 armor - the target-side Carve debuff was not seen by this damage instance. Understated by exactly the 30% reduction.
step_3_which_value_the_wiki_demands.new_value_109.8: mitigated at 63.70 armor = 91.00 * (1 - 0.30), matching S1 and S4/S5 exactly.

step_4_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.hypothesis: Bloodsong's 8% Expose Weakness applied twice (1.08^2 = 1.1664, inside the rounding band).
step_4_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.rejected_because: S2 describes one debuff on the target granting one 8%/5% amplification; a second multiplicative application has no source. It also requires a melee Bloodsong holder, while the exact-armor solution above (5% ranged) reproduces BOTH endpoints to the last decimal with no double counting.

step_4_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.hypothesis: The new value double-applies the 30% Carve reduction (armor A -> 0.49A), which would need A = 130.1 and would make the OLD value correct.
step_4_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.rejected_because: No champion in data/champions.json has 130.1 armor at level 18 (nearest values are 127.0 and 132.4; the [129.3, 130.9] band is empty), whereas the single-application hypothesis lands on Annie's armor of exactly 91.00. A double application would also contradict S1's 'up to 30% at 5 stacks' cap.

step_4_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.hypothesis: A Black Cleaver stack-averaging retune (0.8*max_stacks -> exact Cesaro mean, the P3 candidate flagged in S7).
step_4_alternatives_considered_and_rejec.rejected_because: Arithmetically impossible: that model's whole reduction range is 18%-30%, whose maximum achievable damage ratio is bounded by 0.82/0.70 = 1.171 only as armor -> infinity; at the maximum reachable champion armor (141) the ratio is at most 1.056. Step 1 shows the required armor would be ~5200.

conclusion: The golden leaf's +16.68% change is exactly the 100/(100+R) consequence of applying Black Cleaver's 5-stack 30% armor reduction (a target-side debuff, therefore shared across the roster) to a damage instance that previously used the target's unreduced armor: 179.81 raw -> 94.14 at 91.00 armor vs 109.84 at 63.70 armor. The new value is the wiki-correct one.
